messages:
Dylan Brooks: Kicking off a quick thread on two things for guided onboarding: (1) feature flag targeting rules (beta cohorts) and (2) where checklist state lives (client vs server). We need to align before we lock the implementation.

Chloe Martin: +1. We can ship the UI shell behind a flag either way, but state model depends on this. Also we need to support reset for support/internal.

Jada Williams: I dropped an ADR draft in Confluence. WIP but has the decision points + tradeoffs:
https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ARCH/ADR-0137-onboarding-checklist-state-and-validation

Hannah Rivera: Reading now. Question: are we assuming per-org or per-project state? UX spec seems per project, but some steps are org-wide (API key creation).

Dylan Brooks: My preference: state stored server-side per (org_id, project_id) with step-level granularity, but allow some steps to be “org-scoped” (e.g. created first API key) and automatically satisfy across projects. We can represent scope in the step definition.

Ethan Park: Agree w/ server-side. Client-only is going to get flaky the moment someone uses multiple browsers or the SDK from CI. Also, “first successful request” validation requires backend signal anyway.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: Re: API keys — keys are org-level objects but can be “prod” vs “test” labeled. If the step is “Create a prod key”, that’s org scope and should mark complete for all projects.

Chloe Martin: Makes sense. Implementation detail: we should avoid “fanout write” updating every project row when an org step completes. Better to compute effective completion at read time (project state + org state overlay).

Jada Williams: Yep, ADR proposes:
- state tables: onboarding_checklist_state_project + onboarding_checklist_state_org
- API: GET returns merged view (org steps + project steps)
- step definitions include `scope = org|project` in code/config

Logan Wright: From telemetry side: please keep step completion events idempotent. We’ll get duplicates from retries / refresh. Use a deterministic dedupe key: (org_id, project_id, step_id, completion_source).

Nadia Rahman: +1. Also: do NOT pass any prompt content or request bodies in events. If “first successful request” is validated, emit just model_id (if allowed) + route + latency bucket, but no text. We’ll enforce allowlist server-side.

Amara Diallo: For “first successful request” validator: do we validate off gateway logs or metrics? If metrics, there’s a lag. UX should account for eventual consistency (e.g. “this may take up to 1–2 min”).

Dylan Brooks: Good call. Let’s bake “pending validation” state into the step UI so it doesn’t look broken.

Hannah Rivera: On feature flag targeting: are we using our internal Flags service or LaunchDarkly? For cohort targeting (new orgs + allowlist + %), internal seems fine but need the “new org” detection.

Ethan Park: Use internal Flags. We already have org-created-at in auth service, so targeting rule can be “org_age < N days” + allowlist + random %. But we need a stable bucketing key (org_id) so users don’t churn in/out.

Chloe Martin: Also need a manual override for support: enable/disable for specific org regardless of cohort (esp to debug). Maybe a Console admin panel or internal endpoint.

Cole Summers: Random % rollout should be per org (not per user) to avoid inconsistent experiences. If usage/quota step is in the checklist, we don’t want half an org seeing it.

Jada Williams: ADR currently proposes these targeting modes:
1) allowlist orgs (explicit)
2) “new orgs only” (created_after timestamp)
3) percentage rollout (hash(org_id) mod 100)
4) global off switch
And “support override” stored in DB to short-circuit flag.

Logan Wright: Please ensure the override path is auditable. We’ve had issues where flags got flipped in prod without breadcrumbs. Even a simple audit log row (who/when/what) helps.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: One more nuance: if the checklist is off, should we still collect telemetry events? I’d vote yes for baseline measurement but mark `checklist_exposed=false`.

Nadia Rahman: Yes, but sampling rules differ. If we collect without UI exposure, we should be careful not to balloon event volume. Maybe only collect key funnel events (api_key_created, first_successful_request) at 100%, and UI-specific events only when exposed.

Dylan Brooks: Sounds right. Action items:
- Jada: update ADR with org/project overlay approach + “pending validation” UI state + audit log note.
- Ethan/Hannah: confirm internal Flags supports (new org + allowlist + % rollout) with stable bucketing.
- Chloe: propose state schema + API shape (GET merged, PATCH per scope) and how reset works.

DeployBot: deploybot APP  — Noted: `onboarding_checklist` flag currently set to OFF in prod, ON in staging. :information_source:

Chloe Martin: Re reset: should be admin-only and should clear both org+project state + any “validator derived” completion? For derived, we should probably not store “derived” as a write, but as computed from signals.

Jada Williams: Exactly. ADR angle: only store explicit completion when it’s user-driven/manual. For validator-driven steps, store “last_seen_signal_ts” and compute completion if signal exists. That way reset doesn’t fight the validator.

Amara Diallo: +1, otherwise “first successful request” could re-complete immediately after reset because logs still exist. If we use “first seen after checklist enabled” semantics, we need a cutoff timestamp.

Ethan Park: Hmm. If we do cutoff, we’ll lose real completion for existing orgs in beta. Maybe simplest: completion = exists(any success request) regardless of when. Reset is for UX troubleshooting only, and we can warn support it may re-complete fast.

Dylan Brooks: Let’s keep semantics simple for beta. We’ll document in the support runbook: reset may immediately re-trigger validator steps. Longer-term we can add cutoff per flag enablement if needed.

Hannah Rivera: Cool. I’ll sync w/ Flags team and confirm we can express “org_created_after” + allowlist + % + override without code changes.

Logan Wright: When you update ADR, tag me/Nadia so we can sanity check the event implications.

Dylan Brooks: Will do. Thanks all.
